steps.content: [Saffar's Dream, use any WhiteSands background]
When dry winds caressed his face, they sometimes stirred memories of home.

Every year, when the air grew crisp, the oleaster tree by his home would sag under the weight of its fruit, small and dark red, bursting with sweetness. No matter how many they ate, there were always more.
But the tree was gone now. His home had long since vanished, swallowed by DisCity's artillery fire.

The escape was a slow unraveling. Water ran low. Hard biscuits crumbled to dust in his hands. The line of refugees stretched thinner each day, their numbers dwindling as the weak collapsed into the sand. When his parents could go no farther, they pressed their last scrap of food into his palm and faded into the white dunes.
Hunger gnawed at him, sharp and relentless. Yet worse than the ache in his stomach was the certainty—this exile had no end.

steps.speaker: Researcher
steps.content: Huh? A refugee who actually made it here alive...

steps.speaker: Researcher
steps.content: Can't even speak anymore? You're too consumed by Mania. You don't have long left.

steps.speaker: Researcher
steps.content: Food? Even if I gave you something to eat, it wouldn't matter. The Mania's already taken you.

steps.speaker: Researcher
steps.content: However...

steps.speaker: Researcher
steps.content: There is actually a way... Do you want to live?
After enduring agony that seared down to his marrow, a group of white-coated figures crowded around him. Their voices were buzzing with excitement, talking about another successful test subject.
Metal fused with his flesh, replacing what Mania had rotted away. His stomach no longer twisted with hunger; his body was no longer wrapped in rags.
...Yet the gnawing fear of starvation clung to him. Old habits died hard—he still hoarded scraps of food like a feral thing.
Thwack! A sharp blow cracked against the back of his skull.
Someone lurked in the shadows above him. It was a small figure, probably another kid his age.
She tossed something absently in her hand as she spoke, her voice dripping with arrogance.
Hey, you've got food. Why aren't you eating it?
Hey—Hellooo—? Huh, are you stupid or something?
Only survivors get food. They need you alive for now, so relax, they don't starve you.
You really are stupid. Only survivors get food. They need you alive for now, so relax, they don't starve you.
Her lip curled in contempt, then a flicker of realization crossed her face. When she spoke again, her voice was honeyed poison.
You survived, but do you know what happened to the ones who didn't?
Hehe, they all died!
Or—even worse—they turned into monsters! Now they just wander around, eating people to stay alive. Sooo... scared yet?
...Tsk, you're no fun. Can't even freak you out.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: There are things way scarier than monsters.

steps.content: Hunger, disease, calamities, war... Compared to those horrors, imaginary monsters are nothing, and this place is as close to heaven as it gets.
Really? I'd actually like to go see for myself. I've never been outside. Those white coats don't let me out.
Hey, what's your name?
What a weird name—sounds like some girl's. Mine's way cooler: Synex. Now that's villain material!
Synex flicked the thing in her hand toward him. This time, he caught it. It was an oleaster berry.

steps.speaker: Synex
steps.content: That's your payment! Tell me more about the outside world next time, <color=#fb9259>Saffar</color>!
[Fade to black, center text]

That oleaster berry had shriveled skin and didn't taste good. Honestly, it was barely edible. But I could never forget it. After that, every time we met, Synex would bring a few of the same dried berries. At first, I assumed they were the only ones available at the research institute. Only later did I learn that she, as the facility's experimental subject with the highest resonance rate, had the privilege of choosing her own food. And yet, she deliberately picked the toughest ones.
[Scene Transition]

One oleaster berry for one story. I'm still alive, though with my low Aurum Secretum resonance, insignificance was always my fate. Meanwhile, Synex's brilliance only grew brighter. In time, she earned the right to step beyond these walls. She became a legend at the Fraser Institute, a force to be reckoned with. And so, she no longer needed my stories of the outside world.

Life went on this way. Synex would return from time to time, bringing meager snacks and hauling away trinkets and scraps in trade. One by one, the others who had entered the institute with me died. And as their numbers dwindled, so too did Synex's visits, stretching longer between each appearance. Until...
[Scene Transition: Laboratory]

steps.speaker: Laboratory Guard
steps.content: Damn it! Stop her! Backup! We need backup NOW—

Red warning lights strobed violently, casting jagged shadows as chaos erupted through the laboratory. With a feral snarl, Synex wrenched herself free from her shackles, the sheer force of her movement sending shockwaves ripping through the room.

A predator unleashed, she lunged onto the rubble of collapsed walls, her claws carving through the air like scythes as she descended upon the high-ranking man. Her lips were peeled back in a grotesque rictus, less a smile than a snarl of pure, unfettered madness.

steps.speaker: Synex
steps.content: Kill me... or... I'LL KILL YOU!!

Around her, Aurum Secretum surged in molten waves, forming an impenetrable barrier—a domain of her own making. This was not the Synex he knew. And yet, in this moment of monstrous abandon... it was as if he was seeing her for the very first time.

But she still failed. Her body crumbled like sand, piece by piece—too weak to even lift a claw toward Campbell's throat. Yet, he didn't hold it against her. Instead, he pardoned her. Drew her into the fold of the Campbells. At last, she was truly part of Fraser.
After that, Synex didn't appear for a long time. But sometimes, in the quietest moments, her voice would still whisper in my mind.

steps.speaker: Synex
steps.content: Is the life of your <color=#fb9259>hero</color> as worthless as a stray dog's?
[Scene Transition: Fraser Institute Exterior]
When Synex finally showed up, she brought two unwelcome visitors from DisCity with her.
DisCity origin, directly involved in the West District BR-002 incident. Affiliated with the MBCC, maintains close ties to SHP-13. A potential intelligence asset regarding the shackles.
Small and frail... yet her eyes burned with defiance. As expected, she infiltrated the institute, desperate to save Synex, only to fail.
Too weak to succeed. Too powerless to change anything.
...Just like me. We are the same.
Many came, hoping to become the next "Synex." They entered the institute, but few survived the resonance process.
They are just like me. For them, Synex's oleaster berries are an unattainable dream. This is the only lifeline within their reach. I want them to succeed. I want to help them.
After all... this is the last thing I can do.
[Black Screen Transition, Background: Fraser Institute Corridor - Day]
The young man opens his eyes.
The weight of recent days presses down like storm clouds. Forgotten memories tear through the fragile peace of his mind. Even in rare moments of stillness, they come unbidden.

steps.speaker: Researcher
steps.content: The DisCity Sinner has escaped, but she won't get far. We're tracking her down as we speak.

steps.speaker: Researcher
steps.content: You don't look well, sir... Maybe you should get some more rest?

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: ...No, I'm good.

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: Let's go. Time to meet our rebellious "hero."
